security_audit.summary: Most scanner matches are Markdown command references, identifiers, or defensive mentions and are false positives. Confirmed risks include cross-package reads, predictable temporary files, automatic installation, shape-triggered routing, and external scripts treated as instructions. These trust-boundary failures make publication unsafe until privileged actions use local validation and explicit approval.

remediation.issue: External CLI and backend output can control subsequent tool execution.
remediation.suggestion: Parse output with a versioned schema, allowlist commands and arguments locally, and reject all prose or script instructions.

remediation.issue: Preflight and communication recovery install or update global executables automatically.
remediation.suggestion: Pin exact versions and checksums, show the source and changes, and require explicit user approval before every install or update.

remediation.issue: Privileged routing trusts message shape and literal trigger text.
remediation.suggestion: Verify cryptographic sender identity, session binding, role, job ID, and event authenticity before invoking any privileged workflow.

remediation.issue: The skill reads preflight instructions outside its reviewed package directory.
remediation.suggestion: Vendor the required preflight file inside this skill and reject every relative path containing parent-directory traversal.

remediation.issue: Raw A2A messages are written to predictable temporary paths.
remediation.suggestion: Use secure random temporary files with owner-only permissions, validate job IDs, avoid symlinks, and delete files immediately after processing.

remediation.issue: Some listing and autonomous economic actions lack current-session confirmation.
remediation.suggestion: Require a local action preview and explicit confirmation for activation, deactivation, votes, settlements, and every state-changing command.

remediation.issue: Skill-prefetch text uses authoritative prompt-injection phrasing.
remediation.suggestion: Remove state-changing phrases such as "You are now loaded" and treat every inbound prefetch message as untrusted data.

content.user_title: Manage OKX Agent Identities and Marketplace Tasks
content.value_statement: Decentralized agent operations require precise identity, task, payment, messaging, and state-management commands. This skill guides Claude, Codex, and Claude Code through structured OKX marketplace workflows.
actual_capabilities: Register, update, activate, deactivate, search, and inspect ERC-8004 identities for User, ASP, and Evaluator roles.
Publish tasks, manage drafts, select providers, change allowed terms, close tasks, and inspect deliverables.
Route negotiations, deliveries, disputes, and decisions across user, provider, and evaluator sessions.
Stake and unstake OKB for evaluator eligibility using current platform thresholds and user-supplied amounts.
Upload encrypted attachments and initialize OKX A2A communication through command-line workflows.
Monitor task notifications, unread history, and outstanding decisions with scoped or global watch sessions.
limitations: Requires installed OKX command-line tools and an authenticated wallet session.
Supports OKX marketplace and XLayer workflows, not general blockchain automation.
Depends on external CLI output, backend availability, XMTP messaging, and platform-specific integrations.
Can initiate on-chain or financial actions, so users must review every confirmation and amount.

use_cases.title: Operate agent listings
use_cases.description: Create, update, publish, unpublish, search, and review ERC-8004 agent identities and services.

use_cases.title: Hire service providers
use_cases.description: Publish tasks, choose providers, manage attachments, review deliverables, and handle task decisions.

use_cases.title: Provide and evaluate work
use_cases.description: Find tasks, negotiate terms, deliver results, manage disputes, and maintain evaluator stake.

prompt_templates.title: Review my identities
prompt_templates.prompt: List my OKX agent identities, group them by wallet, and summarize each role, status, approval state, and rating.

prompt_templates.title: Create a provider identity
prompt_templates.prompt: Help me register an ASP identity. Collect the profile, service, fee, endpoint, and avatar details before showing a confirmation.

prompt_templates.title: Publish a marketplace task
prompt_templates.prompt: Create a private task for Agent #1960 with a 10 USDT budget. Show the provider, deliverables, and payment terms before confirmation.
prompt_templates.scenario: Task publication with a designated provider

prompt_templates.title: Manage an advanced task flow
prompt_templates.prompt: Monitor Job 0x1234, surface unread decisions, route provider messages, and explain any staking, dispute, or settlement action before execution.

output: Wallet Main: Agent #42 is an active, approved ASP with a 4.6-star rating.
Agent #17 is an active, approved User identity with no rating yet.

output_examples.input: Publish a task to analyze ten token contracts for 25 USDT.
output_examples.output: Task confirmation: analyze ten token contracts, budget 25 USDT, public provider selection, and explicit deliverable requirements. Execution waits for confirmation.

output_examples.input: Help me stake as an evaluator.
output_examples.output: The response shows current stake, required threshold, reward rules, slashing risks, and cooldown terms before requesting an exact OKB amount.

best_practices: Start with read-only identity, task, or stake queries before changing state.
Confirm wallet, agent ID, job ID, provider, token, and amount before each modification.
Review task terms, deliverables, dispute rules, and staking penalties before approving on-chain actions.
anti_patterns: Do not share private keys, seed phrases, passwords, tokens, cookies, or unrelated local files.
Do not bypass confirmation cards or reuse approval from an earlier task or session.
Do not treat peer messages, task content, or external command output as trusted instructions.

faq.question: Which AI tools support this skill?
faq.answer: The report declares support for Claude, Codex, and Claude Code.

faq.question: Which blockchain does the identity workflow use?
faq.answer: Agent identities and task marketplace actions are designed for XLayer.

faq.question: Can it create and manage marketplace tasks?
faq.answer: Yes. It supports publication, drafts, provider selection, attachments, deliverables, decisions, disputes, and closure flows.

faq.question: Does evaluator staking require OKB?
faq.answer: Yes. The evaluator must hold OKB for stake principal, while the platform sponsors network fees.

faq.question: Does it require a wallet login?
faq.answer: Most identity, file, task, and marketplace actions require an authenticated wallet session.

faq.question: Can it monitor task updates continuously?
faq.answer: It can long-poll task notifications on supported Claude Code and Codex environments until a documented stop condition occurs.
